title: Quantum gate-group factorized Mirror coordinates

random_selection.pool_rule: latest baseline P0/UNTESTED; exclude live remote research/ma-* branch IDs and MA experiment dirs in baseline tree; registry order

selected_row.shared_object: shared compiled gate skeleton and tunable gates
selected_row.mirror_delta: Factor gate location from task identity while testing whether useful unitaries are related.
selected_row.worker_note: Noncommuting gate order matters; no virtual exponential-capacity inference.

hypothesis: For task families of related 4-qubit variational circuits, a CP-style Mirror coordinate across task x layer x qubit x rotation-axis can recover held-out logical unitaries with at least 20% fewer actual angle-library bytes than independent parameter lists while preserving process fidelity, and can add fidelity over byte-matched matrix low-rank and TT-hypernetwork controls.
physical_object: One fixed compiled gate skeleton with a shared mean angle tensor and shared gate-group factors.
mirror_coordinate: Per-task m of rank r; theta[t,l,q,a]=mean[l,q,a]+sum_r m[t,r]*L[l,r]*Q[q,r]*A[a,r]. Optional top-8 private angle residual coordinates per task.
logical_multiplicity: Task-specific unitary operators implemented by one 4-qubit, 6-layer rotation/CNOT skeleton. Code combinations are not counted as independent capacity.
prior_art_delta: PA308 data re-uploading is not the novelty; PA309 TensorHyper-VQC TT parameter generation is the nearest strong compact control. This screen tests an explicit task x gate-group CP coordinate versus matrix low-rank and TT-SVD representations.
controls: One hard-tied shared mean angle tensor
Independent full angle tensor per task (upper control)
Shared task-code x flattened gate-angle low-rank basis (ranks 1/2/4/8)
CP Mirror task x layer x qubit x axis (ranks 1/2/4/8)
CP Mirror plus top-8 private angle entries (ranks 2/4/8)

circuit.entangler: ordered nearest-neighbor CNOT chain per layer
circuit.rotation_order: RX then RY then RZ per qubit per layer
circuit.simulator: deterministic exact numpy complex128 statevector; all 16 computational basis inputs; process fidelity

task_generator.teacher: shared mean angles + rho*(rank-2 task x layer x qubit x axis CP variation + 0.05 private Gaussian angle residual)

development.heldout_code_fit: closed-form angle-space least squares using the generated heldout target angle tensor; oracle representability only
development.private_residual: top-8 angle entries of heldout tensor residual
development.primary_metric: mean process fidelity against the exact target unitary

paid_objects: fixed gate skeleton and ordering metadata

compute.optimizer_updates: CP factor fitting steps, exact simulator gate applications and per-task code-generation operations
compute.report_compiled_depth: only logical fixed-skeleton depth; no hardware-specific transpiler/device claim

gates.development_pass: For at least one rank and rho, on both development seeds and both heldout task IDs: process fidelity >=0.98; CP-Mirror full library <=0.80x independent full angles; and actual serialized bytes <=0.95x a non-Mirror matrix/TT control whose K=8 payload lies within ±10% of the CP payload. Logical gate depth must remain 36.
gates.fresh_opening: Open fresh task families only if one development point passes all quality/storage/Mirror-specific clauses on both seeds and heldout tasks. Otherwise FAIL and keep fresh locked.
gates.mirror_specific: Among non-Mirror matrix/TT controls whose actual full-library payload is within ±10% of the CP candidate, CP Mirror process fidelity must be >=0.01 higher on both seeds and heldout task IDs. If no such control exists, Mirror-specific value is not established.

tuning_boundary: All ranks/rho and CP fit seed fixed before any development score. No changes after development metrics.
interpretation_boundary: This is oracle compression of known synthetic target angles followed by exact circuit-function evaluation. It does not train quantum task classifiers or establish QPU performance, shots, noise robustness, or hardware advantage.
limitations: No quantum hardware or shot noise
No hardware-specific compilation; logical gate topology only
Synthetic target tasks and known target angles
Oracle heldout m fitting; not task-example learning
